questions.q: Which standard object is the only one that can use a Hierarchical Relationship field?
options: Account
Opportunity
User
Contact
questions.explain: Hierarchical Relationship is a special Lookup available only on the User object, typically used to build a management chain.

questions.q: A custom object needs to reference 'its own parent of the same type' — not a User manager chain. What relationship type handles this?
options: An External Lookup Relationship
An ordinary self-referencing Lookup Relationship
This cannot be modeled in Salesforce
A Hierarchical Relationship
questions.explain: Hierarchical is restricted to the User object. Any other object models its own hierarchy with a regular self-referencing Lookup, like Campaign's Parent Campaign field.

questions.q: What does an External Object represent?
options: A deprecated object type no longer supported
A custom object with no fields
Data that physically lives outside Salesforce and is accessed live rather than stored locally
A standard Salesforce object that has been renamed
questions.explain: External Objects represent data stored outside Salesforce, typically accessed live through a connection like Salesforce Connect.

questions.q: An External Lookup Relationship matches records using what, instead of a standard Salesforce record ID?
options: A formula field
The record's created date
A record's Owner field
An External ID field identifying the record in the outside system
questions.explain: External Lookup Relationships match against an External ID field rather than a Salesforce record ID, since the related record doesn't live in Salesforce's own storage.

questions.q: Once an External Lookup Relationship is set up, how does its related list compare to a standard Lookup's related list?
options: It requires a separate Salesforce license to view
It only shows a single record, never a list
It looks and behaves almost identically, aside from columns like External ID and Display URL
It cannot be displayed on a page layout at all
questions.explain: The related list is designed to look and feel like any other related list, so users don't need to know whether the data is stored in Salesforce or fetched live from elsewhere.
